Why Theale Green School?
At Theale Green School, we believe in unlocking potential and inspiring excellence in every student. Our vibrant and supportive community nurtures academic success, creativity, and personal growth, ensuring students leave confident and ready for the future. With engaging lessons, fantastic extracurricular opportunities, and a strong focus on individual development, we create an environment where students thrive and achieve their best. Whether it’s through top-tier teaching, sports, performing arts, or leadership programs, Theale Green empowers students to dream big and succeed. Join us and be part of a school that’s dedicated to your future!

Parent Coffee Mornings – Your Voice Matters!
We love welcoming parents to experience a day in the life of our students! Our Coffee Mornings with Mrs. Badarello provide a fantastic opportunity to see lessons in action, engage in open discussions, and share your thoughts on key topics.
Want to get involved?
Email: headpa@thealegreen.w-berks.sch.uk
Charlotte Badarello
It is a great privilege to be the Headteacher of our wonderful community at Theale Green School and I am delighted that you are interested in finding out more about what we have to offer. Although we are the fastest growing secondary school in West Berkshire, we have protected the warm family feel of our community by ensuring year group numbers remain small.
I know that selecting a school for your child is one of the most important choices to make, and I hope we can give you a flavour of our dynamic learning environment and our welcoming, inclusive community. We are a listening school and use our regular Headteacher & parent coffee mornings to give parents valuable insight and receive feedback to shape our community.
Theale Green School parents are clear that they chose our school confident that their child will be known, and supported, to becoming the unique and special person they have the potential to become. To quote a recent parental survey: “I have always felt that Theale Green is a school where students are encouraged to be who they want to be… Your school really does offer the students so much”.
2025 has seen our community strengthen and thrive more than ever, with many Theale Green School students joining having had their parents and grandparents come through the school. Our students are shining brighter than ever before and are rightly proud of their school.
We look forward to welcoming you to Theale Green School – we know you will love it as much as we do.

Theale Green School was judged to be at the ‘Expected Standard’ in five categories, and our safeguarding standards were fully met.
Ofsted saw, and were able to understand, our school’s journey of school improvement. This is testament to our fierce determination as a community for Theale Green School to thrive and provide pupils with the best possible school experience. The inspectors enjoyed visiting our “friendly school” and understood that our wonderful pupils embrace every opportunity and develop into well-rounded young adults.
“Pupils are proud to be part of this small and friendly school.”
“Pupils are known, supported and cared for.”
“Leaders maintain high expectations. They focus intently on reducing barriers to pupils’ learning and wellbeing.”
“Students are well prepared for education, employment or training.”
A new Ofsted framework (from September 2025)
Ofsted introduced a new Inspection Framework and Evalutation Toolkit in September 2025, bringing important changes to how schools are inspected.
It’s important to understand that the new framework is not directly comparable to the previous inspection system.
We want to make sure all families understand what this means.
What has changed?
Previously, school’s received one overall grade but now schools are assessed across multiple areas. There is no single overall judgement and instead reports are presented as a ‘report card’.
The new grading system
Each area is graded using the following scale:
Safeguarding is graded simply as Met or Not Met
What does a “Needs Attention” grade really mean?
This should be viewed like an MOT advisory. It highlights an area that would benefit from further focus but does not indicate a serious concern. It is expected that many schools may have one or more areas labelled this way as part of normal continuous improvement.
Exceptional – Among the very best nationally
Strong Standard – Above expected standards
Urgent Improvement – Immediate change required
What does Ofsted inspect?
Ofsted grades eight key areas:
Safeguarding (reported as Met / Not Met)
Inclusion
Achievement
Attendance & Behaviour
Personal Development & Well-being
Post-16 Provision
Leadership & Governance

Inclusion Department – SEND
Transforming Lives Through Learning
At Theale Green, our SEND department – Inclusion – is dedicated to opening doors for all students, fostering a belief in their self-worth, and nurturing their independence and life skills. We are committed to building the character of kindness in each individual, ensuring that every student feels valued and empowered.
We believe that the future belongs to them, and our goal is to create happy, balanced and considerate students who are well-prepared for all transitions in life. We support our students in developing meaningful relationships and connections, guiding them to become compassionate and resilient members of society.
Together, we strive to create an inclusive environment where every student can thrive and reach their full potential.
The Inclusion Team is led by Claire Lloyd – Assistant Headteacher – SENCo, who is supported by Ashleigh Kidd Deputy SENCo & Head of Year 8. In addition, we have two higher level learning mentors who run our Lexia Literacy Program as well as a team of learning mentors who either support in lessons or run targeted programmes for students.
Learning Mentors add value by understanding the needs of the student and ensures that support is effective. Learning Mentors will circulate the classroom, providing help and support to develop independent learners which prompts critical thinking. Learning Mentors are integrated into the overall teaching and learning strategy of the school. This includes providing appropriate training and ensuring they understand the curriculum and the specific needs of the students they support.

Theale Green School Celebrates National Sporting Success with Fifth Consecutive Platinum School Games Mark Award
Theale Green School is celebrating an extraordinary sporting achievement after being awarded the prestigious Platinum School Games Mark Award for the fifth consecutive year.
The award places Theale Green School among an elite group of schools nationally. Out of more than 25,000 primary and secondary schools across England, only 190 schools have achieved the Platinum Award for five years in a row, highlighting the school’s unwavering commitment to sport, physical activity and student wellbeing.
The School Games Mark is a government-led award scheme, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust, which recognises schools for their commitment to providing high-quality sporting opportunities and promoting active lifestyles. The Platinum Award is the highest accolade available and celebrates excellence across participation, competition, leadership, inclusion and physical wellbeing.
Theale Green School has consistently demonstrated its dedication to ensuring all students have access to a wide range of sporting opportunities, encouraging participation at every level while developing young leaders, volunteers and role models through sport.
This remarkable fifth consecutive Platinum Award reflects the passion, hard work and commitment of the school’s PE and Sport Department, staff, students and wider community.
Mr Blinco, Director of Sport and PE at Theale Green School, said:
“To receive the Platinum School Games Mark for a fifth consecutive year is an incredible achievement and one that everyone connected with the school should be immensely proud of. Sport and physical activity play a vital role in school life at Theale Green and this award reflects the dedication of our students, staff, volunteers and leaders who continually strive to create opportunities for others. Being recognised among such a small number of schools nationally is a testament to the culture we have built and our commitment to helping every young person enjoy and benefit from being active.”
Mrs Badarello, Headteacher at Theale Green School, said:
“We are absolutely delighted to have achieved the Platinum School Games Mark for a fifth year and are incredibly proud to be recognised among the very best schools in the country.
We are especially pleased that this award reflects the wide-ranging opportunities available to our students, enabling them to participate in sport and physical activity in ways that suit their interests, abilities and aspirations.”
The award recognises not only competitive success but also the school’s commitment to inclusion and ensuring that every student has the opportunity to participate in physical activity, regardless of ability or background.
Theale Green School remains committed to inspiring healthy, active lifestyles and providing outstanding sporting experiences both within the curriculum and through its extensive extra-curricular programme.

KS3 Awards Evening – A Celebration of Growth, Achievement and Community
On Thursday 9th October, we were delighted to welcome students, families, and staff to our KS3 Awards Evening a special event celebrating the achievements of our Year 8 and Year 9 students from the 2024/25 academic year. The evening was a joyful reflection of the hard work, character, and commitment shown by our students, and it was wonderful to see so many proud family members in attendance.
Mr Bowler opened the evening with a warm welcome, followed by an inspiring speech from Emily Clifford, a member of our Sixth Form Head Team. Emily shared her personal journey, reflecting on how the foundations for her success were laid during KS3. Her words resonated deeply, reminding us all of the importance of perseverance, self-belief, and embracing every opportunity.
The evening continued with the presentation of awards, with students recognised for Respect and Hard Work across each subject area. These awards highlighted those who consistently demonstrated kindness, professionalism, and integrity in their interactions, as well as those who showed exceptional dedication to their learning and personal growth.
Attendance Recognition Ms Sanders then took to the stage to honour students who achieved 100% attendance last year, a testament to their resilience, dedication, and commitment to their education.
The evening concluded with a series of special awards presented by Miss Kidd, Head of Year 8 and Mr Bowler on behalf of Mr Neill, Head of Year 9.
A Sweet Ending The evening ended with tea, cake, and plenty of smiles, as families and staff took the opportunity to chat, take photographs, and celebrate the incredible achievements of our KS3 students.
We look forward to celebrating with our Class of 2024/25 GCSE students in November, A Level students in January and with our new current Year 7’s in March.

House Quiz Night – Thursday 2nd October
We were very excited to welcome staff, students and parents to House Quiz on Thursday 2nd October. It was an incredible evening that was a perfect night for quiz fanatics.
Following the head scratching preliminary rounds (in which our teams had to name films from their first lines, identify caricatures of famous singers, name artists and titles of album covers and identify nuts before working our whether they were actually nuts) we started the pub quiz rounds. Two of these were written by our House Captains, Maddie and Erin and covered themes such as General Knowledge, Music and the Movies. We were blown away by the incredibly specific knowledge on display during Mastermind with the specialist subjects for our House Captains being Gavin and Stacey, Would I Lie to You, Station 19 and the High School Musical Trilogy. The University challenge round saw teams made up of students from different year groups battle each other in a game of knowledge. There were also two Taskmaster challenges the first saw our brave heads of house trying to throw a tea bag into a cup from the furthest distance. Using a mix of dexterity and cunning (he made the teabag a bit soggy) Mr Chattock won that round.
But it was Benyon that won the Taskmaster team round, in which teams had to work together to make an individual look bigger than they are. Benyon came up with the ingenious idea to use shadows to make their person much bigger than any of the other teams.
It was neck and neck throughout and this was seen in the final score with only one point separating the top three teams but Scott coming out on top!
See you again next year for some more fun and games. Don’t forget that our second House competition – House Performance is on Tuesday 21st October at 7pm. See you there!

Leadership Team
Headteacher – Charlotte Badarello
I know the difference a great teacher can have on shaping people’s lives, and how education can enable dreams to become a reality. I graduated from the University of Bristol and completed my Masters before starting my career in finance. I subsequently retrained as a maths teacher, spending 10 years at a school in West London, before relocating back to Berkshire. I joined Theale Green School in 2019 as Deputy Headteacher, and am incredibly proud of the improvements the school has made. This is my third school and I love the sense of community and purpose that resonates throughout the school. Every student and member of staff is treated as an individual, and these strong connections create well-rounded individuals which is what makes this such a special school. I feel very fortunate to be part of this rapidly improving school and the place it holds in the local community.
Deputy Headteacher – Paul Bullock
Since completing my PGCE at Brunel University, I spent the first ten years of my teaching career in a Buckinghamshire school, joining as a PE Teacher and progressing through a range of curriculum and pastoral roles before joining the leadership team. In 2016 I became Assistant Headteacher of a new school in Berkshire, holding responsibility for the Curriculum, Assessment and Whole School Literacy. I am excited to be joining Theale Green; the passion, positivity and sense of community displayed by staff and students is inspiring, and I am looking forward to becoming part of the school as it continues its journey.
Deputy Headteacher – Matthew Bowler
I really believe a teacher can inspire hope, ignite the imagination, and install a love of life time learning. Having completed my PGCE at the University of Chichester I took up my first teaching post as a PE teacher at a school in Oxfordshire, spending seven years as Director of PE, alongside completing my Masters in School Leadership. I joined Theale Green School in September 2021 as Assistant Headteacher with responsibility for teaching and learning. Instantly being absorbed into the culture of the school, the sense of community and willingness to go above. I look forward to being part of the Theale Green School community.
Assistant Headteacher & SENDCo – Claire Lloyd
With over 25 years teaching experience across primary and secondary, I have seen the many building blocks that go into education and fully appreciate the impact that positive experiences at school can have on the longer term outcomes of students. After completing my degree in Sports Science and Geography from Brunel University, I spent a year in banking. I quickly realised that I wanted to be in a profession that gave something back and so completed my PGCE in Secondary Education (Geography) at Reading University. Following this, I spent the next 15 years teaching at a secondary school in Oxfordshire, with prolonged spells as Humanities Lead and Head of House. Then, I took the position of SENCo at a local West Berkshire Primary School. It was a decision that shaped the next ten years of my life. I am passionate about opportunities for all, about challenging all students to have high aspirations and for every student to feel safe and feel a sense of belonging.
Acting Assistant Headteacher – David Holbrook
I have always been committed to improving student outcomes and helping students achieve their full potential. After graduating from Manchester Metropolitan University with degree in Business, Computing in Education, I relocated to Reading in 2005 and began my teaching career. My experience has been in a diverse range of schools and I have had a range of roles with experience in curriculum and pastoral. I started at Theale Green School in January 2018 and have had the privilege of being part of the positive change seen in the school. I have seen Theale Green School go from strength to strength. The students and the staff make the school an enjoyable place to work and I am focused on the futures of all students in the school.
Assistant Headteacher & Designated Safeguarding Lead – Marianna Tottman
I utterly believe that building and sustaining an inclusive culture, where every student is known and well understood, can be truly life changing. Having graduated in 2004 with a First-Class Honours Degree in Drama from the University of Southampton, I went straight into Teaching, completing my PGCE at Reading University. Since then, I have spent the last twenty years working in a number of secondary schools as a Drama and Dance teacher, Head of Performing Arts and Assistant Headteacher. More recently I have also had experience working as Safeguarding Lead for a multi-academy trust, supporting students and colleagues in both primary and secondary settings. What drew me to Theale Green is the importance the school places on “belonging” and the motivation to achieve excellence through a relational approach.

Welcome to Theale Green School
It is a great privilege to be the Headteacher of our wonderful community at Theale Green School. Theale Green School has a rich legacy, steeped in history from its beginnings as a grammar school, that has evolved, with our house system at the heart of our identity. Our students and families know they are important which builds a strong sense of belonging within our community; I am delighted that you are interested in finding out more about what we have to offer. Although we are the fastest growing secondary school in West Berkshire, we have protected the family feel of our community by ensuring year group numbers remain small.
I know that selecting a school for your child is one of the most important choices to make, and I hope we can give you a flavour of our dynamic learning environment and our welcoming, inclusive community. We are a listening school and use our regular Headteacher & parent coffee mornings to give parents valuable insight and receive feedback to shape our community.
We know the classroom experience is the key to success, and I am proud of the happy, dedicated TGS staff who prioritise strong relationships with their students. Our curriculum is based on the best current educational research available and designed to enable our students to thrive and achieve their personal best. Our student destinations are testament to this, recent alumni include prestigious apprenticeships, top universities leading to careers in the film industry and global accountancy firms.
Theale Green School parents are clear that they chose our school confident that their child will be known, and supported, to becoming the unique and special person they have the potential to become. To quote a recent parental survey: “I have always felt that Theale Green is a school where students are encouraged to be who they want to be… Your school really does offer the students so much”.
2025 has seen our community strengthen and thrive more than ever, with many Theale Green School students joining having had their parents and grandparents come through the school. Our students are shining brighter than ever before and are rightly proud of their school.
We look forward to welcoming you to Theale Green School – we know you will love it as much as we do.
B.Sc (Hons), MA, NPQH

Governance and Policies
The school is governed by a Local Governing Committee made up of unpaid volunteers from the parent body, staff and the local community. They have a range of expertise and skills and they serve on a number of different committees covering all aspects of school life.
The Local Governing Committee’s primary responsibilities are:
Being an academy, Theale Green reports directly to the Department for Education, and not as most local schools do to the West Berkshire local authority.
The Chairman and individual committee members can always be contacted by parents and staff through the Clerk to the Local Governing Committee via email clerk@alet.org.uk
Fancy joining us on our mission to Transform Lives through Learning?
If you want to make a difference in your community and develop your own professional skills, come and volunteer as a school governor and you can do both. We all want the best for children and for our local schools: governors play a key role in leading, supporting and improving these schools, and becoming one can be a very rewarding experience. Plus it may not be as time consuming as you think, and we offer lots of training and support to help you.
Want to know more?
If you’d like to know more about becoming a governor, please contact Heledd Walker, Head of Governance and Compliance via email Clerk@alet.org.uk. We’ll be thrilled to hear from you.

pageCache.text:
Join Us for Our Open Evening!

Our mission, values and learner attributes
Theale Green School is proud to be part of the Activate Learning Education Trust (ALET) group of schools and colleges, united with its vision of ‘Transforming Lives Through Learning’. We believe in the power of education to open doors for all young people. As such, our Teaching and Learning strategy is strong – and it works. We have a proud record of academic excellence, with many of our students achieving outstanding exam results. Almost two thirds stay with us in Sixth Form and go on to top universities or apprenticeships, but more importantly they leave with a sound belief in their self-worth.
We are proud be a ‘Well School’. This is a national initiative led by the Youth Sport Trust to prioritise wellbeing. We aim for every member of our school to know that they are valued as individuals and for them to thrive in an energised, confident and optimistic environment.
Our physical environment is ever-changing. We have invested in the refurbishment of many of our buildings over the last five years, and our students value their modern, accessible facilities. We are delighted that this year students have been able to access our brand new, state-of-the-art Fitness Zone both in PE lessons and after school. We are so proud to have again been awarded the prestigious ‘Youth Sports Trust Platinum Award’ – we are the only school in West Berkshire to win it this year and it’s unprecedented for it to be won three years in a row!
Students at Theale Green School enjoy a broad, balanced curriculum which lies at the heart of our students being well-rounded individuals. We have a well-established heritage of the Creative Arts and Sport, which continues to grow through enrichment opportunities such as Duke of Edinburgh, extra-curricular clubs, leadership programmes and self-development courses.
As well as academic learning, our students practise a range of ‘life skills’ through various experiences which prepare them for life after school, including connections with local businesses and employers.
To Transform Lives Through Learning
Values and learner attributes
We ask our whole school community to embrace our values of Respect, Hard Work and Progress – these are the drivers for daily life at school, and our school behaviour and rewards system is built around these values. Additionally, we proactively teach our learning attributes of Professional, Aware, Enterprising, Resilient and Confident – the characteristics that top employers have told us they value the most in the workplace

Bright futures ahead as Theale Green School students receive A Level and vocational results
Overall, the results for the cohort reflect sustained whole school improvements, with students making better progress compared to national average. Two thirds of grades were A*- C.
There was a fantastic atmosphere around the sixth form as students celebrated their achievements and looked ahead to the future. Staff were on hand to share in their success and provide support to those finalising their plans for September.
Headteacher Charlotte Badarello, said: “we are delighted that so many of this incredible year group have secured their places at prestigious universities and degree apprenticeships. This cohort are the first to join Theale Green School in year 7 as part of the ALET Trust, and have shone brightly in their seven years, contributing significantly to the success of the school. These students have taken on lead roles in school productions and have had significant impact in our community through their whole school leadership roles. These students are now in a strong position to progress their studies further.”
David Holbrook, Assistant Headteacher Sixth Form, said “I am so proud of what this fantastic group of young people have achieved. They are role models for younger students; their tenacity and resilience has left a firm legacy within the school for many years to come. They have strengthened the culture of leadership within the sixth form and have given back to the local community; the best example of this was our hugely enjoyable annual Pensioner’s Tea Party. I wish them all the very best for the future.”
Several students achieved exceptional results and are now heading off to top universities, including:
Apprenticeship success
In addition to those progressing to university, a number of students have secured sought-after apprenticeship placements, including:
Speaking on results day, Emily Clifford, who is heading to study nursing, said:
“I am really excited to start my nursing qualification. I enjoy helping others and am looking forward to starting my career”
For students who are still considering their next steps, the school is offering advice and guidance to support their decision-making in the coming weeks.
Megan Lockley with Thames Valley Police.

GCSE Awards Evening – A Night of Celebration and Achievement
On Thursday evening, we welcomed students, families, and staff to our annual GCSE Awards Evening—a truly memorable occasion to celebrate the hard work, resilience, and success of our Year 11 who sat their exams earlier this year. The hall was filled to capacity, creating a fantastic atmosphere of pride and support.
The programme began with a warm welcome and presentation of GCSE certificates, followed by an inspiring address from our special guest, Steve Frew. Steve, Scotland’s first-ever Commonwealth Games Gold Medalist in Gymnastics, shared his remarkable journey of perseverance and achievement, leaving students and families motivated and uplifted.
We then moved on to the presentation of Subject Awards, which were nominated by subject leaders to recognise students who demonstrated exceptional commitment, progress, and achievement in their chosen subjects. These awards celebrate not only academic excellence but also resilience, creativity, and a positive attitude to learning—qualities that truly embody the spirit of Theale Green School.
The Fine Art Award – Maya Bednarcyzk
The 3D Art Award – Beau Durrant
The Hospitality & Catering Award – Alicia Gushlow
The Photography Award – Willow Hopcroft
The Business Studies Award – Veronica Pieta

Following this, we presented the Special Recognition Awards, highlighting outstanding accomplishments across the year group.
Special Awards
Selwyn Jones Award – Arthur Reeves Named in honour of a passionate Science teacher, this award celebrates resilience and dedication to science. Arthur demonstrated phenomenal progress in Year 11 through hard work and perseverance, achieving two strong passes in a subject he once thought impossible.
Jacqueline Ann Fogg Award for Girls’ Dedication to Sport – Millie Jeanes This award recognizes outstanding commitment to school sport. Millie has represented both school and club from Year 7 to Year 11, inspiring peers through her dedication and serving as a true role model.
Governors’ Cup – Ella Russ Awarded to a student who overcame significant health challenges to achieve strong GCSE results. Ella’s determination and success are now reflected in her thriving Sixth Form journey.
Leadership Team Award – Jack Maynard Chosen by the Leadership Team, this award honors Jack’s resilience and maturity. Despite major barriers, Jack achieved strong GCSE passes, opening doors to a bright future.
Headteacher’s Award – Alastair Cox This award celebrates Alastair’s exceptional personal growth and academic achievement. From creative talents to securing top GCSE grades, Alastair’s journey reflects hard work and ambition, paving the way for an exciting future.
